items.basis: The candidate is not the status quo: it adds a floating basin shade cover and a pre-summer 40 ppm biocide shock to the otherwise unchanged 14 bar / 120-nozzle recirculating loop, so it is a distinct intervention even though its claimed benefit is unsupported. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "floating shade cover on the cooling basin plus one pre-summer biocide shock dosing at 40 ppm with rinse-down" vs baseline "as currently implemented, doing nothing new".

Not impossible as installed, but the sole disclosed failure mode, cover wind damage, has no mitigation or load rating, and a floating cover on a 32-38 C basin also risks reduced evaporative cooling on a loop whose temperature is set by the strip schedule. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "Known failure modes (claimed by the generator): cover wind damage"; EVIDENCE ev:basin-temp ("loop runs 32-38 C year-round (temperature-controlled by the strip schedule").

The acceptance metrics do not match the held record: the prediction requires monthly clog-rate plots and a chlorophyll criterion, while the evidence reports per-campaign events over 12 campaigns and provides no chlorophyll baseline or scale-versus-biofilm split. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "monthly clog-rate plots across two years" / "basin chlorophyll counts stay below 5 micrograms per liter through summer" vs EVIDENCE ev:cloglog-24mo ("24-month nozzle clogging log across 12 campaigns").
